front.title: A SCITT Profile for Verifiable Audit Trails in Algorithmic Trading: The VeritasChain Protocol (VCP)
front.workgroup: Supply Chain Integrity, Transparency, and Trust

abstract.t: This document defines a profile of the SCITT (Supply Chain Integrity, Transparency, and Trust) architecture for creating tamper-evident audit trails of AI-driven algorithmic trading decisions and executions. The VeritasChain Protocol (VCP) applies the SCITT framework to address the specific requirements of financial markets, including high-precision timestamps, considerations arising from recordkeeping regimes such as the EU AI Act and MiFID II, and a crypto-shredding mechanism intended to support erasure obligations such as those under the GDPR. This profile specifies how VCP events are encoded as SCITT Signed Statements, registered with Transparency Services, and verified using COSE Receipts. It further defines SCITT conformance profiles for interoperability and an ERASURE event type that records crypto-shredding operations as append-only audit events. The profile makes trading records auditable and attributable after the fact; it does not prevent or block any trading activity, and it does not warrant the correctness of any recorded decision.

note.name: About This Document
note.t: This is an unsubmitted editor's candidate for discussion. The -07 identifier is provisional. The published revision is -06; this file is not evidence of a new IETF submission, VSO adoption or an implementation-conformance result.
The latest version of this document, along with implementation resources and test vectors, can be found at .
Discussion of this document takes place on the SCITT Working Group mailing list (scitt@ietf.org).
Proposed changes from -06 are listed in . The SCRAPI description and examples are corrected; the six Open Issues remain unresolved. Earlier changes are recorded in the subsequent appendices.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: The SCITT (Supply Chain Integrity, Transparency, and Trust) architecture provides a framework for creating tamper-evident logs of digital artifacts through Transparency Services. While SCITT was initially designed for software supply chain use cases, its core primitives--Signed Statements, Receipts, and Transparency Services--are applicable to any domain requiring verifiable audit trails.
This document specifies a SCITT profile for AI-driven algorithmic trading systems in financial markets. The VeritasChain Protocol (VCP) applies the SCITT architecture with domain-specific extensions:

ul.li: A schema for encoding trading events as SCITT Signed Statements
Registration policies for financial audit trails
Conformance tiers (Silver, Gold, Platinum) with varying requirements for timing precision, anchoring frequency, and key protection
A crypto-shredding mechanism intended to support data erasure obligations
A completeness-aware design that enables omission detection through external anchoring

section.t: VCP serves as an "AI Flight Recorder" for algorithmic trading, supporting post-incident reconstruction of recorded system behavior with cryptographic evidence that the records were not altered after commitment. It cannot reconstruct events that were never recorded.

section.name: Requirements Language
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

section.name: Relationship to SCITT
section.t: This document is a profile of the SCITT architecture. It:

ul.li: REQUIRES compliance with
REQUIRES use of SCRAPI for Transparency Service interactions
RECOMMENDS COSE Receipts for inclusion proofs
DEFINES domain-specific extensions for financial trading

section.t: This profile does not define a new SCITT protocol or new Transparency Service interactions; it specifies how existing SCITT primitives are applied to VCP events in the financial trading domain. The VCP event format and integrity layer are defined in .

section.name: Scope
section.t: This document specifies:

ul.li: VCP Event schema as SCITT Signed Statement payload
Registration Policy requirements for VCP Transparency Services
Mapping of VCP concepts to SCITT terminology
Three conformance tiers with specific requirements
Crypto-shredding mechanism to support erasure obligations
Three-layer integrity architecture

section.t: This document does not specify:

ul.li: General SCITT architecture (see )
SCRAPI endpoints (see )
COSE Receipt format (see )
Specific regulatory mapping (covered in companion documents)
A particular anchoring service (the anchor target is deployment-specific; anchoring itself is REQUIRED)

section.name: Terminology
section.t: This document uses terminology from . The following terms are specific to this profile:

dl.dd: A single auditable record in the VeritasChain Protocol, encoded as a SCITT Signed Statement. Consists of Header, Payload, and Security metadata.
An algorithmic trading system, AI model, or human operator that generates VCP Events. Corresponds to SCITT Issuer.
A SCITT Transparency Service configured with VCP-specific Registration Policies. Operates a VCP-compliant append-only log.
A COSE Receipt issued by a VCP Transparency Service, proving inclusion of a VCP Event in the log.
An entity (algorithm, human operator, or system) identified by ActorID that generates VCP Events.
A privacy technique where encrypted payload data is rendered permanently unrecoverable by destroying the encryption key, while preserving the cryptographic integrity proofs (hashes and Receipts).
One of three implementation levels (Silver, Gold, Platinum) with increasing requirements for timing precision, anchoring frequency, and key protection.

A cryptographic commitment (typically a Merkle root) published to an external, independent system (e.g., public blockchain, timestamping authority). External anchoring makes omission of events from an anchored batch, after anchoring, detectable by third parties at batch granularity.
A field within the VCP Event that explicitly identifies the applicable Registration Policy and conformance tier.

section.name: SCITT Terminology Mapping
section.t: The following table maps VCP concepts to SCITT terminology:

tr.td: VCP Event is the payload of a Signed Statement
COSE Receipt with Merkle inclusion proof

section.name: Architecture
section.t: VCP builds upon the SCITT architecture with domain-specific extensions for financial trading:
section.artwork: +------------------+ +-------------------------+ | VCP Issuer | | VCP Transparency | | (Trading System) | | Service | +--------+---------+ +------------+------------+ | | | 1. Create VCP Event | | 2. Sign as COSE_Sign1 | | | +------ Signed Statement ----->| | (via SCRAPI) | | | 3. Validate against | | Registration Policy | | | | 4. Append to Log | | |<-------- VCP Receipt --------+ | (COSE Receipt) | | | +--------+---------+ +------------+------------+ | Verifier | | External Anchor | | (Auditor/Regul.) | | (Timestamp/Blockchain) | +------------------+ +-------------------------+

ol.li: Event Generation: VCP Issuer creates a VCP Event containing trading decision or execution data.
Signing: Event is signed using COSE_Sign1 with the Issuer's private key.
Registration: Signed Statement is submitted to VCP Transparency Service via SCRAPI POST /entries.
Validation: Transparency Service validates against VCP Registration Policy.
Logging: Valid statement is appended to the append-only log.
Receipt: COSE Receipt with Merkle inclusion proof is returned to Issuer.
External Anchoring: The Merkle root MUST be periodically anchored to an external system at the frequency of the applicable tier (), making post-anchor omission detectable by third parties.

section.name: Per-Actor Hash Chain (Optional)
section.t: VCP MAY maintain per-Actor hash chains in addition to SCITT's global append-only log. When implemented, each VCP Event includes a PrevHash field containing the hash of the previous event from the same Actor. This enables efficient verification of a single Actor's event sequence without downloading the entire log.

Note: Per-Actor hash chains are OPTIONAL. External anchoring of batch roots provides the primary mechanism for completeness verification at batch granularity. Hash chains serve as a complementary local integrity mechanism.
section.artwork:
Actor A: Event_A1 --hash--> Event_A2 --hash--> Event_A3
Actor B: Event_B1 --hash--> Event_B2
Global Log: [Event_A1, Event_B1, Event_A2, Event_B2, Event_A3, ...]

section.name: Three-Layer Integrity Architecture
section.t: VCP defines a three-layer architecture that separates concerns and clarifies where each integrity property originates:

tr.td: Individual event authenticity via digital signature
Merkle root anchored to external system

section.t: Note: Layer 3 (External Verifiability) is REQUIRED at every tier, as in VCP v1.2 . Revisions -02 and -03 of this document described it as OPTIONAL at the protocol level; that description did not match the VCP specification and is withdrawn. Lightweight or delegated anchoring mechanisms are acceptable at the Silver tier.

External anchoring makes post-anchor omission detectable: without it, a log producer could rebuild a batch and publish a different Merkle root. Anchoring lets third parties check a presented root against an independently recorded commitment, supporting the "Verify, Don't Trust" principle. It does not reveal events that were never included in a batch.

section.name: VCP Event Schema
section.t: A VCP Event is encoded as the payload of a SCITT Signed Statement. The payload MUST be a JSON object conforming to the following schema:

section.name: Header Object
section.t: The Header contains metadata common to all VCP Events:

dl.dd: REQUIRED. UUID v7 providing time-sortable unique identification.
REQUIRED. ISO 8601 timestamp with nanosecond precision.
REQUIRED. Integer timestamp in nanoseconds since Unix epoch. Values exceed 2^53, so a parser that does not preserve 64-bit integer precision alters them. See regarding canonicalization.
REQUIRED. Registered event type code (see ).
REQUIRED. Identifier of the entity generating this event.
REQUIRED. Identifier of the per-Actor hash chain.
REQUIRED. Monotonically increasing sequence number within the Actor's chain.

REQUIRED. Identifier of the Registration Policy under which the event is registered. Per VCP v1.2 , PolicyID SHOULD follow the Issuer Domain + Local ID convention (reverse_domain:local_identifier), for example "org.veritaschain.policy:gold-v1-2". Global uniqueness is achieved through domain ownership; no central PolicyID registry is operated.

section.name: Payload Object
section.t: The Payload contains domain-specific data organized into modules:

dl.dd: Trading data: orders, executions, modifications, cancellations.
Risk management data: exposure, limits, margin.
Governance data: algorithm parameters, decision factors, operator actions.
Privacy metadata: encryption keys, retention policies.

section.name: Security Object
section.t: The Security object contains integrity and chaining information:

dl.dd: REQUIRED. SHA-256 hash of the canonicalized Header and Payload, computed using JSON Canonicalization Scheme .
OPTIONAL. Hash of the previous event in this Actor's chain. If present, MUST match the EventHash of the preceding event (except for INIT events where it is absent).
OPTIONAL in individual events. Included in anchor (ANC) events.

REQUIRED. Signature algorithm identifier. MUST be "ED25519" (default) or "DILITHIUM2", the VCP v1.2 registry value for ML-DSA . DILITHIUM2 carries EXPERIMENTAL status in VCP v1.2 and is intended for testing and hybrid (classical plus post-quantum) deployments; it is not a certification requirement.
OPTIONAL. Reference to the anchor location (e.g., blockchain transaction ID, TSA receipt ID), populated once the batch containing the event has been anchored. See on the corresponding field in .

section.name: SCITT Alignment Object
section.t: VCP v1.2 defines an OPTIONAL SCITTAlignment object carried in the Header. It makes the binding between a VCP Event and its SCITT artifacts (Signed Statement, Transparency Service, Receipt) explicit and machine-readable.
Field presence is governed by conformance profiles:
Implementations claiming the VCP_SCITT profile MUST include the SCITTAlignment object in every registered event; this profile-based approach avoids partial-implementation ambiguity.

dl.dd: REQUIRED when present. VCP specification version governing the alignment semantics ("1.2").
REQUIRED when present. One of "VCP_BASE", "VCP_SCITT", or "VCP_REGULATORY".
OPTIONAL. Identifier of the SCITT Signed Statement carrying this event.
OPTIONAL. Identifier of the Transparency Service with which the event is registered. REQUIRED under the VCP_SCITT profile.
OPTIONAL. Receipt encoding in use; "COSE_RECEIPT" designates COSE Receipts as specified by the SCITT architecture .
OPTIONAL. Structured reference to the Registration Policy (PolicyID, Issuer, IssuedAt) mirroring the Header-level PolicyID.

section.name: Event Types

tr.td: ERR_CONN, ERR_AUTH, ERR_TIMEOUT, ERR_REJECT, ERR_PARSE, ERR_SYNC, ERR_RISK, ERR_SYSTEM, ERR_RECOVER
Recorded chain reset with authorized recovery action (Payload.VCP-RECOVERY)

section.t: The five SYS_* codes were registered by the VCP v1.2 release; their structured payload locations and runtime requirements are defined in the normative annex of . Validators written against pre-release v1.2 artifacts need updating to accept them.

section.name: Registration Policy
section.t: A VCP Transparency Service MUST enforce a Registration Policy that validates incoming Signed Statements.

section.name: Policy Identification
section.t: The PolicyID field MUST be explicitly included in the VCP Event Header. The Transparency Service MUST validate the registration request against the referenced Registration Policy and MUST NOT infer, select, or substitute a policy on its own.
PolicyID values SHOULD follow the Issuer Domain + Local ID convention defined in VCP v1.2 : the reverse DNS notation of the Issuer's domain, a colon, and an issuer-defined local identifier. Examples:

ul.li: org.veritaschain.policy:silver-v1-2
org.veritaschain.policy:gold-v1-2
org.veritaschain.policy:platinum-v1-2

section.t: Uniqueness derives from domain ownership; no central PolicyID registry is operated. Organizations without a domain MAY use a "local:" prefix at the cost of weaker uniqueness.

Conformance tiers (Silver, Gold, Platinum) represent additional verification depth and operational requirements applied on top of the same core Registration Policy, and do not define separate or incompatible registration policies.

section.name: Validation Requirements
section.t: The Registration Policy MUST verify:

ol.li: Schema Compliance: Payload conforms to VCP Event schema.
PolicyID Present: Header contains a valid PolicyID field.
Signature Validity: COSE_Sign1 signature is valid for the registered Issuer public key.
Timestamp Validity: TimestampInt is within acceptable bounds (not in future, not too old).
Chain Integrity (if PrevHash present): PrevHash matches the hash of the most recent event from this Actor.
Sequence Monotonicity: SequenceNum is exactly one greater than the previous event's SequenceNum.

section.name: Tier-Specific Requirements
section.t: This specification distinguishes timestamp resolution from clock accuracy. Nanosecond-resolution timestamps represent the storage format capability, while actual clock accuracy is explicitly recorded and enforced per tier.

Note: Silver tier is NOT intended for regulatory-grade algorithmic trading systems subject to MiFID II RTS 25, SEC Rule 17a-4, or equivalent clock synchronization requirements. Silver tier is appropriate for development, testing, backtesting analysis, and non-regulated trading scenarios.

section.name: Certification Policy Requirements
section.t: This document does not mandate a specific external anchoring service; it requires anchoring at the frequency of each tier. Each AnchorRecord binds the batch Merkle root, event count, first and last event identifiers, and PolicyID (see on the scope of the AnchorRecord signature). Implementations retain local copies of all AnchorRecords and document an anchor continuity plan, as defined in .

Certification programs may impose requirements beyond this profile, such as multiple independent anchors. Certification requirements are defined separately from this document and may evolve independently of it. Implementations may conform to this profile without obtaining certification.
Acceptable anchor targets include:

ul.li: Trusted timestamping authorities (TSA) per
SCITT Transparency Services, with COSE Receipts per
Public blockchains (e.g., Bitcoin, Ethereum)
Public timestamping services and attested databases, at the tiers where permits them

section.t: A time-stamping authority attests existence time; by itself it does not show that the same root was presented to every verifier.

section.name: Crypto-Shredding
section.t: VCP supports crypto-shredding as a technical mechanism that can support erasure obligations while preserving audit trail integrity. It renders protected plaintext irrecoverable without invalidating cryptographic proofs. Whether it satisfies a specific legal obligation is not determined by this document.

ol.li: Encryption: Sensitive payload fields are encrypted with a per-record or per-subject Data Encryption Key (DEK).
Key Storage: DEK is stored separately, indexed by SubjectID.
Hashing: EventHash is computed over the encrypted payload, preserving integrity.
Shredding: Upon erasure request, DEK is destroyed. Encrypted data becomes unrecoverable.
Verification: Receipt and hash chain remain valid--verifiers can confirm event existence and ordering without accessing decrypted content.

section.name: ERASURE Event Type
section.t: VCP v1.2 defines the ERASURE event type to reconcile erasure obligations (such as GDPR Article 17) with append-only, tamper-evident audit trails. An ERASURE event does not delete or rewrite any prior event. It records, as a new append-only event, that the plaintext of specified protected fields has been rendered irrecoverable through crypto-shredding (destruction of the Data Encryption Key), while the EventHash, Merkle inclusion, and external anchor of the target events remain verifiable.

In the VCP v1.2 release, an ERASURE event MUST carry its details in Payload.VCP-PRIVACY.ErasureDetails, with the seven REQUIRED members below. ErasureDetails at the event root or directly under Payload is invalid. The flat ERASURE fields described in -03 of this document (ErasureTargetEventIDs, ErasureReason, KeyDestructionProof, RetentionExemption, OperatorID) reflected pre-release artifacts and are not a v1.2 encoding. Historical signed data is not rewritten. The normative annex of states how pre-release records are handled; it defines no lossless automatic conversion to the v1.2 encoding.

tr.td: Type (ACCOUNT, SESSION or EVENT_RANGE), salted SHA-256 Hash, and Salt
AffectedEventCount, FirstAffectedEventID, LastAffectedEventID and AffectedFields; EventIDs MAY enumerate the exact affected set
Code, Description, LegalBasis and a SHA-256 RequestReferenceHash
Authorizing role, signature, nanosecond timestamp and DPO notification
SHA-256 hash of the key identifier, key algorithm, destruction method and nanosecond destruction timestamp

section.t: Reason codes are GDPR_ART_17_1A, GDPR_ART_17_1B, GDPR_ART_17_1C, GDPR_ART_17_1D, RETENTION_EXPIRED, SUBJECT_REQUEST, COURT_ORDER and ERROR_CORRECTION. Destruction methods are HSM_ZEROIZE, SECURE_DELETE and CLOUD_KMS_DESTROY. Authorization MUST precede or equal destruction, which MUST precede or equal the ERASURE event timestamp. The ERASURE event's own Merkle inclusion proof is detached (Evidence Pack or Receipt), not embedded in its hashed payload. Schema validation checks the structure of this evidence, not the truth of the destruction.
The following abbreviated example follows the structure of the release fixture; hashes, signatures and certificates are placeholders:

ERASURE provides a technical mechanism that supports erasure obligations; it is not a legal determination. Whether crypto-shredding qualifies as erasure under a given regime is jurisdiction- and case-dependent. Deployments subject to reproduction-oriented recordkeeping rules (such as SEC Rule 17a-4 audit-trail controls) should note that once a DEK is destroyed the original plaintext is, by design, not re-creatable. Where a retention duty prevents deletion, a successful ERASURE event is not emitted for data that remains decryptable. The legal basis and any retention override recorded with an erasure require verification outside the event schema .

section.name: SCRAPI Integration
section.t: VCP Transparency Services MUST implement SCRAPI . The descriptions below follow revision -11 of that API; they do not define alternative SCRAPI resources.

section.name: Registration (POST /entries)
section.t: A client submits a COSE_Sign1 Signed Statement carrying the VCP event to the registration resource defined in Section 2.3 of . The Transparency Service applies its Registration Policy before further processing.
section.sourcecode:
POST /entries HTTP/1.1 Host: vcp-ts.example.com Accept: application/cbor Accept: application/cose Content-Type: application/cose
<COSE_Sign1 containing VCP Event payload>
section.t: A successful synchronous registration returns the Receipt in a 201 response. An accepted asynchronous registration returns 202 while the Receipt is pending. In both cases the Location header identifies the Receipt resource. A 202 response is not evidence that registration is complete or that a Receipt has been issued.

section.name: Receipt Resolution (GET the Location URL)
section.t: The client follows the Location URL returned by registration, for example /entries/{EntryID}, as defined in Section 2.4 of . This resource returns a Receipt, not the original VCP event. A 200 response carries the COSE Receipt; 204 indicates that registration is still pending; 404 indicates that no Receipt exists, including a failed registration. Polling and error handling follow SCRAPI.
This profile defines no derivation of EntryID from Header.EventID. The client uses the service-provided Location instead of synthesizing a Receipt URL from an event identifier.

section.name: Receipt Verification and Statement Availability
section.t: The Receipt resource is the Location URL described above; this profile does not append a /receipt suffix. Obtaining a Receipt is separate from verifying it against the candidate Signed Statement and the trusted service context. The unresolved context questions are recorded in , item 6.

The original Signed Statement and any detached payload are supplied to a verifier through the applicable evidence-distribution or artifact-repository mechanism. The SCRAPI Receipt resource does not provide an event-download API.

section.name: External Anchor Information
section.t: External anchor evidence, such as a blockchain reference or timestamp token, is made available through the deployment's documented evidence-distribution mechanism. This profile does not define GET /anchors/{anchor_id} as a SCRAPI resource. A deployment-specific anchor-status API is outside this profile; its response is not by itself verification of the anchor.

section.name: Integrity Architecture
section.t: VCP's three-layer architecture provides defense in depth:

ul.li: Layer 1 (Event Integrity): Digital signatures on individual events make forgery without the signing key detectable.
Layer 2 (Collection Integrity): Merkle trees enable efficient proof of inclusion.
Layer 3 (External Verifiability): External anchoring makes post-anchor omission detectable by enabling third parties to check presented Merkle roots against independent records.

section.t: The optional per-Actor hash chain provides additional local integrity checks but is not required for external verifiability.
Mitigations against key compromise:

ul.li: Frequent Merkle anchoring to external append-only stores
HSM-based key storage (Platinum tier requirement)
Key lifecycle management under the deployment's documented policy. This profile does not define a ROTATE event or a key-rotation protocol.

section.name: Quantum Resistance
section.t: Ed25519 signatures are vulnerable to attacks by cryptographically relevant quantum computers. VCP provides crypto-agility to address future threats:

ul.li: SignAlgo field enables algorithm negotiation and migration

The DILITHIUM2 registry value (ML-DSA ) holds EXPERIMENTAL status in VCP v1.2: available for testing and hybrid (classical plus post-quantum) deployments, with Ed25519 remaining the default and no certification requirement attached
Hash chain integrity based on SHA-256 provides approximately 128-bit post-quantum security against Grover's algorithm

section.t: Implementers requiring post-quantum assurance SHOULD monitor CFRG and PQUIP working group outputs for updated guidance on algorithm selection and migration timelines.

section.name: Timing Attacks
section.t: Clock manipulation can enable backdating of events. Mitigations:

ul.li: Compare the UUID v7 millisecond timestamp with TimestampInt at millisecond precision. Neither producer-supplied value is an independent attestation of the event time.
Transparency Service enforces timestamp bounds
Platinum tier requires PTPv2 synchronization
External anchoring provides independent timestamp attestation

section.name: Privacy Considerations
section.t: VCP Events may contain sensitive trading information. Operators SHOULD:

ul.li: Use crypto-shredding for personal data subject to GDPR
Implement access controls on Transparency Service queries
Consider encrypted payloads for highly sensitive data

section.name: Completeness Considerations
section.t: SCITT provides inclusion proofs but does not by itself establish completeness (i.e., that no events have been omitted). VCP adds the following:

ul.li: Sequence numbers enable detection of gaps within an Actor's chain
External anchoring of batch roots, with AnchorRecords binding event count, first and last event identifiers and PolicyID, enables third-party detection of omission after anchoring
Heartbeat events (HBT) provide liveness signals that support detection of extended omission periods

section.t: These mechanisms make omission detectable at batch granularity and within the anchoring window; they do not establish that every event that occurred was recorded. An event that was never recorded is detectable only through another record that implies it, such as an order without a corresponding acknowledgment or a counterparty record. The completeness window implied by the tier's anchoring frequency should be disclosed when records are presented.

section.name: Open Issues
section.t: A comparison of the VCP v1.2 integrity layer with the VAP v1.2 framework requirements, published as an unadopted research observation record , identified items 1 to 5 below. Item 6 was added in revision -06. None of them is resolved by this candidate.

ol.li: Local batch Merkle construction. requires Merkle tree construction to follow RFC 6962, but its reference code duplicates an odd node, which yields roots that differ from those of for batch sizes that are not a power of two, and its audit path generation omits that node. Which construction governs, and how roots already computed with the reference code are treated, is not decided by this revision. The question concerns local batch trees only: inclusion in a SCITT Transparency Service's log is shown by COSE Receipts under the verifiable data structure that the Transparency Service uses.

AnchorRecord signature scope. The reference signing procedure signs the Merkle root bytes only, so the event count, endpoints and PolicyID carried in the AnchorRecord are not covered by that signature. The signed bytes of the AnchorRecord remain to be defined.

Integer timestamps. TimestampInt and other nanosecond values are JSON integers that can exceed 2^53, whereas requires numbers to be expressible as IEEE 754 doubles and recommends encoding larger integers as strings. Values that are not exactly representable as a double, such as the TimestampInt 1773567000123456789 in , cannot be canonicalized by RFC 8785 without changing them.
EventHash notation. Examples and fixtures write EventHash with a "sha256:" prefix, while the reference computation yields a bare hexadecimal digest.

Security object fields. This document names the anchor reference AnchorRef, lists MerkleRoot as OPTIONAL in individual events, and has no MerkleIndex. In , the specification text names the field AnchorReference and lists AnchorReference, MerkleRoot and MerkleIndex as REQUIRED from VCP v1.1, whereas the v1.2 JSON schema accepts both AnchorRef and AnchorReference and treats the three fields as VC-Certified requirements enforced by Registration Policy rather than as protocol-level requirements. The canonical name and the requirement level are not decided by this revision, and the fields here are unchanged.

Receipt verification context. Receipt resolution in is separate from verification; builds on inclusion. For the RFC9162_SHA256 verifiable data structure, a Receipt of inclusion signs the Merkle tree root as its payload, under a protected header that identifies the signature algorithm and the verifiable data structure; the tree size and leaf index are carried in the unprotected header, and verification applies the inclusion proof to the bytes of a candidate entry (Section 5.2.1 of ). leaves the specific verifiable data structure to the Transparency Service (Section 5.1.3), and notes that leaf construction can differ by data structure (Section 4). This profile does not yet state (a) which bytes form the entry for a registered VCP Signed Statement and how a verifier learns that rule for a given Transparency Service, (b) which Receipt-signing key a verifier is expected to trust for that service, or (c) what a verifier checks when an argument depends on a statement's position in the log or on the log's size, as omission reasoning can. Because the tree size and leaf index are outside the signed protected header, they are authenticated only through recomputation of the signed root; whether that suffices for such arguments, or whether a signed tree head or consistency proof under a trusted log key is also required, is not decided by this revision. The hackathon report presented to the SCITT Working Group at IETF 127 names the same three points as rules that verifying Receipts across operators currently needs out of band .

section.t: Since -05, VSO's change-proposal register has listed proposed identifiers for change proposals on items 1 to 5 : VCP-CP-2026-003 proposes errata notices for items 1 to 3; VCP-CP-2026-004 proposes a byte contract and migration that covers items 1 to 4, with the numeric-field inventory VCP-CP-2026-005 as an input; item 5 depends on VCP-CP-2026-002 (precedence among the normative annex, the specification text, the JSON schema and examples) and VCP-CP-2026-006 (native field layout). The interim change-control procedure under which these proposals would be decided, VCP-CP-2026-001, was itself under public review when this revision was prepared, and the identifiers take effect only if that procedure is accepted. All of these proposals are unadopted. This document will follow their outcome and does not anticipate it.

section.name: Implementation Status
section.t: Note to the RFC Editor: please remove this section before publication.

This section records the status of known implementations at the time of posting, following . The listing of any individual implementation here does not imply endorsement by the IETF, and the information presented here has not been verified by the IETF. Other implementations may exist.

ul.li: There are no known external implementations of this profile or of VCP.

VSO publishes first-party implementations: VCP-RTA, a reference implementation of VCP v1.1 event logging at the Silver tier, and proof-of-concept repositories for cTrader, FIX, Interactive Brokers, Nasdaq and Cloudflare. VCP-RTA does not produce COSE_Sign1 Signed Statements or register them with a Transparency Service, and it does not implement VCP v1.2. The proof-of-concept repositories have not been assessed against this profile.

VSO also publishes a first-party, pre-release offline library for VCP v1.2 events in Python, TypeScript and MQL5 . It computes canonical hashes, RFC 6962 Merkle roots and inclusion and consistency proofs, Ed25519 event and root signatures, and reports verification results as valid, invalid or indeterminate. It does not read COSE or SCITT envelopes, so it does not implement this profile, and it has not been assessed against it. Where VCP v1.2 is ambiguous, including item 1 of , the library records its own reading; those readings are not VSO change-control decisions.
No Evidence Pack produced under VCP has been accepted in any regulatory, judicial, or audit proceeding.

front.title: Key words for use in RFCs to Indicate Requirement Levels
Ambiguity of Uppercase vs Lowercase in RFC 2119 Key Words
An Architecture for Trustworthy and Transparent Digital Supply Chains

abstract.t: Traceability in supply chains is a growing security concern. While Verifiable Data Structures (VDSs) have addressed specific issues, such as equivocation over digital certificates, they lack a universal architecture for all supply chains. This document defines such an architecture for single-issuer signed statement transparency. It ensures extensibility and interoperability between different transparency services as well as compliance with various auditing procedures and regulatory requirements.

front.title: Supply Chain Integrity, Transparency, and Trust (SCITT) Reference APIs

Improving Awareness of Running Code: The Implementation Status Section

abstract.t: This document describes a simple process that allows authors of Internet-Drafts to record the status of known implementations by including an Implementation Status section. This will allow reviewers and working groups to assign due consideration to documents that have the benefit of running code, which may serve as evidence of valuable experimentation and feedback that have made the implemented protocols more mature.

This process is not mandatory. Authors of Internet-Drafts are encouraged to consider using the process for their documents, and working groups are invited to think about applying the process to all of their protocol specifications. This document obsoletes RFC 6982, advancing it to a Best Current Practice.

This document describes version 2.0 of the Certificate Transparency (CT) protocol for publicly logging the existence of Transport Layer Security (TLS) server certificates as they are issued or observed, in a manner that allows anyone to audit certification authority (CA) activity and notice the issuance of suspect certificates as well as to audit the certificate logs themselves. The intent is that eventually clients would refuse to honor certificates that do not appear in a log, effectively forcing CAs to add all issued certificates to the logs.
This document obsoletes RFC 6962. It also specifies a new TLS extension that is used to send various CT log artifacts.
Logs are network services that implement the protocol operations for submissions and queries that are defined in this document.

front.title: CBOR Object Signing and Encryption (COSE) Receipts

abstract.t: CBOR Object Signing and Encryption (COSE) Receipts prove properties of a Verifiable Data Structure (VDS) to a verifier. VDSs and associated Proof Types enable security properties, such as minimal disclosure, transparency, and non-equivocation. Transparency helps maintain trust over time and has been applied to certificates, end-to-end encrypted messaging systems, and supply chain security. This specification enables concise transparency-oriented systems by building on Concise Binary Object Representation (CBOR) and COSE. The extensibility of the approach is demonstrated by providing CBOR encodings for Merkle inclusion and consistency proofs.

section.name: Changes from draft-kamimura-scitt-vcp-02
